theme: The 〜と conditional — automatic, natural consequences ("whenever / if X, then Y")
intro: 〜と links a condition to a result that always or automatically follows — ideal for directions and how things work.

grammar.title: The 〜と conditional

rules.label: Verbs
examples: 行く → 行くと (iku to) → if/when you go (行く → iku to (if you go))

rules.label: い-adjectives
examples: 安い → 安いと (yasui to) → if it's cheap

rules.label: な-adj / nouns
examples: 静か → 静かだと (shizuka da to) → if it's quiet

grammar.bigPoint: The second clause can't be a command, request, invitation, or want — use 〜たら for those. 〜と is for facts, directions, and instructions only.

vocab.en: to come into view / be visible

examples.jp: まっすぐ 行くと、右に えきが 見えます。
examples.romaji: Massugu iku to, migi ni eki ga miemasu.
examples.en: If you go straight, the station comes into view on the right.

examples.jp: この ボタンを 押すと、きっぷが 出ます。
examples.romaji: Kono botan o osu to, kippu ga demasu.
examples.en: When you press this button, a ticket comes out.

note: 〜と is your go-to for directions ("turn at the corner and you'll see…") and how things work. It also fits natural truths: 春になると、さくらが さきます。(When spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom.) If you want a request or wish after it, switch to 〜たら.

selfCheck.q: How would you say: "If you turn left at the traffic light, the hotel is on the right"?
selfCheck.a: 信号を 左に 曲がると、ホテルが 右に あります。(Shingō o hidari ni magaru to, hoteru ga migi ni arimasu.)
